subject.title: feat(onboarding): unified empty-state with provider icons, websites, and recommended installs

question: Should OpenClaw permanently curate a static cross-vendor recommended-tools catalog in core, or should each provider/runtime owner contribute install recommendations through generic manifest or detector metadata?
rationale: Both designs are technically possible, but they establish different long-term product endorsement, ownership, update, plugin-compatibility, and security responsibilities that cannot be inferred safely from the patch alone.

options.title: Use owner-contributed metadata
options.body: Extend the generic manifest or detector contract so each provider/runtime owns its recommendation, eligibility, website, and artwork while core only aggregates and renders it.

options.title: Approve a core-curated catalog
options.body: Keep the static catalog but explicitly assign its editorial owner, inclusion criteria, platform eligibility rules, URL review process, and update cadence.

options.title: Split the presentation change
options.body: Land only provider presentation metadata and defer the cross-vendor recommended-install catalog until its product ownership is settled.

recommendation.title: Use owner-contributed metadata
recommendation.body: Extend the generic manifest or detector contract so each provider/runtime owns its recommendation, eligibility, website, and artwork while core only aggregates and renders it.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice defines the product's onboarding recommendations and permanent core-versus-plugin ownership boundary.
